The sum of odd numbers 1 through 199 has 100 terms, so the sum is $100^2 = 10000$. Since $10000 = 7 \cdot 1428 + 4$, the remainder is $4$.

Checking the proposed solution: it claims 28 groups of 7 odd numbers from 1 to 197 plus one extra term 199. But 28·7 = 196 terms, whereas there are only 99 odd numbers from 1 to 197. The correct grouping is 14 groups of 7 (98 terms, 1 to 195) plus 197 and 199. Each group sums to 0 mod 7; $197 \equiv 1$ and $199 \equiv 3 \pmod 7$, giving $1 + 3 = 4$. The proposed answer of 5 is wrong (even its claim that $199 \equiv 5$ is wrong; $199 = 7\cdot 28 + 3$).

VERDICT: REJECT
